'''István Horthy de Nagybánya II''' (born 17 January 1941) is a Hungarian [[physicist]] and [[architect]], son of [[Kingdom of Hungary (1920–46)|Hungarian]] deputy regent [[István Horthy]] and [[Ilona Edelsheim-Gyulai]], and grandson of Admiral [[Miklós Horthy]] who served as [[Regent of Hungary]] from 1920 to 1944. In 1965 he converted to [[Islam]] and took the name '''Sharif Horthy'''. Horthy is a prominent member of the Indonesian spiritual association [[Subud]],<ref>{{Cite book |last=United States Joint Publications Research Service |url=https://archive.org/details/ufiche-test-document_jprs-eps-85-086/mode/2up?q=%22sharif+horthy%22 |title=East Europe Report: Political, Sociological and Military Affairs |date=1985-08-26 |others=Internet Archive |pages=41 |language=English}}</ref> and has translated works by its founder, [[Muhammad Subuh Sumohadiwidjojo|Subuh Sumohadiwidjojo]], into English.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sutton |first=Brenda |title=Sharif Horthy |url=https://www.mythicjourneys.org/guest_horthy.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126091712/https://www.mythicjourneys.org/guest_horthy.html |archive-date=2025-01-26 |access-date=2025-04-29 |website=www.mythicjourneys.org}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Horthy was born on 17 January 1941 in Budapest.<ref name=":0" />

He graduated in 1962 with a degree in physics from [[Oxford University]]. He earned a second degree in Civil Engineering at [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]] in 1966.

== Career ==
He worked as a consulting engineer in England and later in the [[Far East]] where he founded and managed two major Indonesian companies in the fields of consulting engineering, construction, and property development.

== Personal life ==
After years in [[Boston]], Massachusetts, Horthy settled in England. 

He has been married twice: his first wife was Henrietta Josephine Chamberlain; they have five children. Sharif is currently married to Tuti, a [[Javanese people|Javanese]] woman, and lives with her in [[Lewes, East Sussex]].<ref name=":0" />
